note: Hand-curated references for the Dammam -> Latakia journey. 'approx': true means the pin is placed roughly and should be checked. 'game' holds ideas for the Unity project (Arar_Station). People entries are fictional NPC archetypes, not real individuals.

items.name: Level 1 – Muhaiya station (محطة المحيا)
items.desc: First game level. Roadside station on Highway 85 (King Fahd Road / Al Jubail–Arar Hwy) ~6.5 km west of central Hafar Al-Batin, heading to Rafha. Neighbours on the map: Al-Sabeel rest house (استراحة السبيل), Gulf ice factory (معمل ثلج الخليج), Raad Al-Shamal diwaniya (ديوانية رعد الشمال) and Jadara college (كلية جدارة). Location from plus code CW44+8M7.
items.game: Level 1 hub: the player's first stop on the Tapline Road – fuel, prayer, tea and a night at the station before the long empty stretch to Rafha.

refs.t: AramcoWorld (Mar/Apr 1967) – 'The Desert Road': building and paving the Tapline Road from Qaisumah to Turaif
Arab News (30 Mar 2008) – Highway users complain of poor services at rest stops
Saudipedia – Stations of the Basra–Makkah pilgrim route (Hafar Al-Batin was a water stop on it)
Wikipedia – Qaisumah (Tapline company town ~20 km east of Level 1)
Al-Eqtisadiah (20 Dec 2008) – camel market (حراج) at the Umm Ruqaibah festival

images.t: Spring desert around Hafar Al-Batin (uploaded Oct 2007) – ground colour and vegetation reference for the level's surroundings

notes: 2000s highway stops in Saudi Arabia were often criticised in the press for poor food, unclean toilets and weak security (Arab News, 2008) – good mood for a worn, slightly neglected Level 1 station.
Spring around Hafar Al-Batin turns the desert floor green with short grass and flowers (the city is nicknamed 'capital of the spring') – an alternative seasonal look for the level.
Lore hook: Hafar Al-Batin began as a water stop for caravans and pilgrims on the old Basra–Makkah route – Level 1 sits on a road travellers have rested on for centuries.
Qaisumah, the next settlement east, grew as a Tapline company town around its pumping station; its name comes from a native desert herb (Achillea, القيصوم) – a plant you can scatter around the level.

Hafar Al-Batin governorate hosts the Umm Ruqaibah camel festival (مزاين أم رقيبة) in its sands every autumn–winter for about 40 days; in the 2000s it already drew big camel auctions (Al-Eqtisadiah, Dec 2008). Good reason for camel trucks, Bedouin pickups and visitors passing Level 1 in winter.

items.name: Dammam
items.desc: Start of the journey. Capital of the Eastern Province on the Gulf coast; with Khobar and Dhahran it forms the oil-industry metro where the Tapline story begins.
items.game: Opening scene: Gulf humidity, corniche at dawn, loading the truck/car before the long drive north-west.

items.name: Dammam No. 7 – 'Prosperity Well'
items.desc: First commercial oil well in Saudi Arabia (1938), in Dhahran. The oil that later flowed through the Trans-Arabian Pipeline started here.
items.game: Historic prologue location / museum-style flashback.

items.name: Jubail
items.desc: Huge industrial city on the coast; the road leaves the Gulf here and turns inland toward Nairiyah.
items.game: Flare stacks and petrochemical skyline on the horizon at night.

items.name: Nariya (Nairiyah) – Tapline pump station
items.desc: One of the original Trans-Arabian Pipeline (Tapline) pumping stations. Each station was a small company town with housing, clinic and school in the middle of the desert.
items.game: First 'station' archetype – compare with Arar/Badanah station in the game.

items.name: Qaisumah – Tapline pump station
items.desc: Tapline's eastern head station (pipeline built 1947–1950 to Sidon, Lebanon). From here the 'Tapline Road' (Hwy 85) follows the pipe north-west for ~1,000 km.
items.game: Where the player joins the Tapline Road – pipeline markers run beside the asphalt.

refs.t: AramcoWorld (Mar/Apr 1967) – 'The Desert Road': building and paving the Tapline Road from Qaisumah to Turaif

items.name: Hafar Al-Batin
items.desc: Big junction town in Wadi al-Batin, near King Khalid Military City. Known for its large livestock / camel trade.
items.game: Busy truck-stop town: workshops, restaurants, shawarma, tyre shops.

items.name: Hafar Al-Batin livestock & camel market
items.desc: Livestock market area for camels, sheep and goats. Pin is approximate – confirm exact market location.
items.game: Camel market scene: haggling NPCs, pickup trucks with camels in the back.

refs.t: Al-Madina – Hafar Al-Batin camel auction: over 20 million riyals in sales, 1,000+ participants

items.name: Ad-Dibdibah plain – camel grazing
items.desc: Flat gravel plain west of Hafar Al-Batin, used by herders for camel grazing, especially after winter rains.
items.game: Open-desert biome: scattered camel herds, water tanker trucks, herders' tents.

items.name: Rafha
items.desc: Town that grew around a Tapline pump station. Midpoint of the Saudi leg of the road.
items.game: Overnight stop option; old Tapline housing compound.

items.name: Camel crossings – Tapline Road (Rafha–Arar)
items.desc: Long open stretch of Hwy 85 through the Al-Widyan plateau. Free-roaming camels near the road are a known night-driving hazard; fenced sections and camel-crossing signs. Research: over 90% of camel–vehicle crashes happen at night; mitigation has included highway fences, underpasses, reflective signs and luminous straps on camels.
items.game: Night-driving hazard event: camels on the road, hazard lights, warning signs.

refs.t: Okaz – most camel-related road accidents happen at night (KACST research)
Gulf News – camels fitted with luminous straps to reduce road accidents
JEMTAC (2012) – review of camel–vehicle collisions: fences, underpasses, reflective signs

items.name: Arar
items.desc: Capital of the Northern Borders Province. The town grew up with the Tapline and its Badanah pump station. Core location for the Arar_Station Unity project.
items.game: MAIN HUB – Arar_Station.

items.name: Badanah – Tapline pump station (near Arar)
items.desc: Tapline pumping station associated with Arar. Station towns had staff housing, a hospital, schools and an airstrip. Exact site to verify.
items.game: Reference for the station building, fences, water tower, pump halls.

items.name: Turaif
items.desc: Last Tapline pump station town in Saudi Arabia; known as one of the coldest towns in the Kingdom in winter (snow occasionally).
items.game: Cold-night variant: frost on the windshield, heater in the truck cab.

items.name: Al-Hamad / Syrian Desert edge
items.desc: Basalt and gravel desert of the Syrian Desert edge between Turaif and Al-Qurayyat; Bedouin camel and sheep herding.
items.game: Black basalt desert biome – very different look from the sandy east.

items.name: Al-Qurayyat
items.desc: Last Saudi town before the Al-Haditha border crossing; olive farms and salt flats nearby.
items.game: Final fuel/food stop before border paperwork.

items.name: Al-Haditha (SA) / Al-Omari (JO) border crossing
items.desc: Main Saudi–Jordan crossing for this route. Long truck queues, customs inspection, money changers, insurance offices. Check current opening hours/status before travel.
items.game: Border gameplay: passport, customs search, waiting queue, insurance kiosk.

items.name: Jordan Eastern Badia
items.desc: Empty desert between Al-Omari and Azraq, Bedouin herders and camel herds, few services.

items.name: Azraq
items.desc: Oasis town and key truck junction (roads to Iraq, Saudi Arabia and Amman). Many truck stops, tyre shops and restaurants along the main road.
items.game: Oasis + truck junction hub.

items.name: Qasr al-Azraq
items.desc: Black basalt fortress; T.E. Lawrence used it as a base in the winter of 1917–18.

items.name: Azraq Wetland Reserve
items.desc: Remnant of a once huge desert oasis, now a protected wetland with water buffalo and migratory birds.

items.name: Mafraq
items.desc: Northern Jordan town; once an important stop on the Hejaz Railway. Last big town before Jaber.

items.name: Jaber (JO) / Nassib (SY) border crossing
items.desc: Main Jordan–Syria crossing on the Amman–Damascus highway. Closed 2015–2018, reopened Oct 2018. Duty-free zone between posts. Check current status before travel.
items.game: Second border: different uniforms, signs, currency (JOD -> SYP).

items.name: Daraa
items.desc: First Syrian city after Nassib, in the Hauran plain.

items.name: Al-Omari Mosque, Daraa
items.desc: Early Islamic-era mosque in old Daraa.

items.name: M5 highway (Nassib – Damascus – Homs)
items.desc: Syria's main north–south motorway, which the route follows from the border to Homs.

items.name: Damascus
items.desc: One of the oldest continuously inhabited cities. Major stop: old city, souqs, Umayyad Mosque.

items.name: Umayyad Mosque
items.desc: Great Mosque of Damascus (705–715 CE), one of the largest and oldest mosques in the world.

items.name: Souq al-Hamidiyah
items.desc: Covered Ottoman-era market leading to the Umayyad Mosque – textiles, sweets, ice-cream (Bakdash), spices.
items.game: Dense shop street reference: metal roof with bullet-hole light shafts, shop signs.

items.name: Al-Nabk
items.desc: Qalamoun mountain town on the M5; cold high plateau between Damascus and Homs. Monastery of Mar Musa nearby.

items.name: Homs
items.desc: Central Syrian city; the route turns west here through the Homs Gap toward the coast.

items.name: Khalid ibn al-Walid Mosque
items.desc: Ottoman-style mosque in Homs with two tall minarets and nine domes.

items.name: Krak des Chevaliers
items.desc: Crusader castle above the Homs Gap, visible from the Homs–Tartus road (short detour).

items.name: Tartus
items.desc: First view of the Mediterranean. From here the coastal M1 runs north to Latakia.

items.name: Arwad island
items.desc: Only inhabited island of Syria, short boat ride from Tartus; fishermen and boat builders.

items.name: Baniyas
items.desc: Coastal town with an oil refinery and terminal – the Iraqi Kirkuk–Baniyas pipeline ended here (pipeline theme continues).

items.name: Jableh
items.desc: Small coastal city with a Roman theatre, 25 km before Latakia.

items.name: Ugarit (Ras Shamra)
items.desc: Bronze-age port city just north of Latakia, where one of the earliest alphabets was found.

items.name: Latakia
items.desc: End of the journey: Syria's main port city on the Mediterranean.
items.game: Final scene: sea, port cranes, corniche at sunset.

items.name: NPC: long-haul truck driver
items.desc: Archetype: driver hauling goods Gulf -> Jordan/Syria, sleeps in the cab at truck stops, knows every tea stand on Hwy 85.
items.game: Gives rumours about camel crossings and border queue times.

items.name: NPC: Bedouin camel herder
items.desc: Archetype: herder with a pickup, water tank and herd near the highway; tent, coffee (gahwa) and dates.
items.game: Offers gahwa; quest to find a lost camel near the road.

items.name: NPC: retired Tapline station worker
items.desc: Archetype: old man who worked at the Badanah/Arar pump station in the 1950s–70s; remembers the company houses and the airstrip.
items.game: Story-teller NPC for Arar_Station lore.

items.name: Roadside tea stand & bakala
items.desc: Archetype: small kiosk at a fuel station – tea, karak, water, snacks, phone cards, sometimes tyre repair next door.
items.game: Shop prefab template for every stop.

items.name: NPC: customs officer & money changer
items.desc: Archetypes at the border: customs inspector, insurance seller, money changer, porters.

items.name: NPC: souq merchant
items.desc: Archetype: Damascene shop owner – textiles, sweets, spices; tea for customers.

items.name: NPC: Latakia / Arwad fisherman
items.desc: Archetype: fisherman at the port, nets and small wooden boats.

items.name: SASCO station – Hafar Al-Batin/Rafha road
items.desc: SASCO roadside service station near Rafha on the Hafar Al-Batin–Rafha international road: fuel, catering (تموين) and lodging (إيواء) on a 15,000 m² site. SASCO announced a 5.5 million riyal redevelopment in August 2017, so a station was already operating here before. Pin placed roughly at Rafha's eastern approach – exact site to verify.
items.game: Template for a bigger 'full-service' stop: fuel + mini-market + restaurant + rooms for truckers and families.

refs.t: FX News Today – 'SASCO reveals development of a new station for 5.5 million riyals' (2017)
